text:
A: Hey, how's it going? Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes, hello. I can hear you. Tomasz.
A: Jago. Nice to meet you, mate.
B: Nice to meet you. Er, I think I already heard about you, actually. The documentary, with the boats? And the release forms?
A: [laughs] Oh no. Tereza's been talking, has she? Yeah, that's me. In my defence, I've got them all signed now. Most of them.
B: Most of them. [laughs] Okay. In my job, "most of them" is a problem, you know?
A: Yeah, fair. What is it you do?
B: Operations manager. Facilities management, for office buildings in west London and Heathrow. Cleaning, security, maintenance contracts. I have six site supervisors. Company car, lots of emails, phone never stops.
A: Proper grown-up job, then. That's the bit I'm dreading, to be honest, the actual career part. I'm in my last year, and all my mates from school are in London already, in offices, and I'm still here doing bar shifts on a Saturday.
B: How old are you?
A: Twenty-three.
B: Twenty-three is nothing. At twenty-three I was cleaning offices at night. I came here at nineteen with, er, one bag. Then porter, then supervisor, step by step. So you are not behind, I think.
A: Oh, that's mad. From cleaning to running the whole thing? That's a proper story, that. I'm not even joking, that's the kind of thing I'd want to film.
B: [laughs] Nobody wants to watch film about toilets on fourth floor.
A: You'd be surprised, mate. People love behind-the-scenes stuff. Actually, does your company do any video? Like, recruitment videos, or showing clients what you do? Because that's exactly the sort of branded content I want to get into after I graduate, documentary-style, real people, not cheesy stock footage.
B: Er, we have one video on website, it's very old. Some man in a suit walking in a corridor. To be honest it's terrible.
A: See, I could sort that. Just saying. I've got a Sony FX3, gimbal, drone licence, the lot.
B: Okay, maybe. I can mention to the directors. I'm not promising, yeah? It's a budget question.
A: No, course, no pressure. Do you get much time off, with all that?
B: Gym three mornings, before work. Saturday I take my daughter swimming. And once a year we go all-inclusive, Crete or Turkey. Last year I booked the premium room, sea view, private pool. Very nice.
A: Private pool, look at you. I've only ever done hostel bunks. Interrailing, five weeks, Lisbon, Berlin. Slept on a floor in Prague one night.
B: No, no, no. I did the floors when I was young. Now I want the good hotel. [laughs]
A: That's earned, though, isn't it, honestly. Do you follow any football? I play five-a-side on a Wednesday.
B: Brentford, a little bit, because it's local. Sometimes a supplier gives us tickets for a box.
A: A box! Mate, you're living the dream. I watch the rugby in the pub with a—
